rule: Attacker should succeed when the opposed grapple check equals or exceeds the defender where the rule says attacker equals/exceeds.
currentEvidence: SWSEGrappling.grappleCheck() uses atkRoll.total > defRoll.total and returns on ties.
resolutionNotes: Math Integrity Freeze, Batch 1 round 7. A shared decision authority (resolveOpposedGrappleOutcome(), exported from grappling-system.js) now uses attackerTotal >= defenderTotal, used by both grappleCheck() (also the basis for attemptPin()) and _opposedGrappleForManeuver() (Trip/Throw's shared helper). grappleCheck()'s tie-specific early return (which discarded an already-true attackerWins on a tie) was removed. See docs/audits/v2-math-integrity-authority-ledger.md's Grapple domain, Certification-correction addendum 7, and tests/opposed-grapple-tie-authority.test.mjs.

rule: Grabbed targets cannot move and take -2 to attacks except natural/light weapons; no generic Reflex penalty is part of the baseline Grabbed state.
resolutionNotes: Math Integrity Freeze, Batch 1 round 7. GrappleStateEngine's Grabbed and Grappled states no longer carry any ActiveEffect changes -- the flat -5 Reflex change is removed entirely, matching the real rule (no Reflex penalty; the -2 attack-roll-except-natural/light-weapon penalty remains a separate, not-yet-automated item, not a Reflex-math defect). See tests/grapple-state-defense-effects.test.mjs. Note the -2 attack penalty itself is still unimplemented and is a genuinely separate, deferred item (not tracked by this ledger entry, which was specifically about the wrong Reflex penalty).

rule: Pinned prevents actions and removes Dex bonus to Reflex; Pin does not force the target to the bottom of the condition track by itself.
currentEvidence: _applyState('pinned') adds -10 Reflex and overrides system.conditionTrack.current to 5.
resolutionNotes: Two parts. The condition-track-override half was already SUPERSEDED before round 7: GrappleStateEngine.advancePair()'s 'pinned' branch carries an explicit comment ('Do not mutate condition track here: Pin is a control state, not CT damage') and does not touch system.conditionTrack at all -- confirmed by direct reading of the current source, not by this evidence's original -10 Reflex/CT-override description (which the code no longer matches; the Reflex value had also already drifted from -10 to -5 by round 6, still wrong in kind). The Reflex half is FIXED in round 7: Pinned no longer applies a flat ActiveEffect change at all -- DefenseCalculator.calculate() now computes a component-aware removal of exactly the actor's positive Dexterity bonus (never a Dex penalty), mirroring the same philosophy already certified for flat-footed Reflex. See docs/audits/v2-math-integrity-authority-ledger.md's Grapple domain, Certification-correction addendum 7, and tests/grapple-state-defense-effects.test.mjs.

rule: Escaping Grabbed, Grappled, and Pinned use different procedures.
currentEvidence: escapeGrapple() uses the same opposed grappleCheck() path and clears both actors on success.
resolutionNotes: This entry's own currentEvidence is stale: escapeGrapple() no longer calls grappleCheck() at all -- it routes through dedicated _escapeWithGrapple()/_escapeWithAcrobatics() methods (each with their own opposed-check-vs-a-strict->-comparison, deliberately left unchanged by round 7: unlike initiating a grapple, an ESCAPE attempt is the one already-in-control party's status quo being contested, so a tie correctly favors the grappler retaining control -- not the same 'meets or beats' rule as grapple-opposed-meets-beats above). Whether Grabbed/Grappled/Pinned SHOULD use procedurally different escape mechanics (different skill options, different DCs) per RAW is a genuine, still-open workflow question, not a wrong-number defect -- explicitly left deferred per the round-7 review's own allowance for workflow-only Grapple limitations.

rule: Visible combat actions should route to the canonical grapple state machine.
currentEvidence: Combat action data has Grapple / Grab text but no clear resolutionMode/handler metadata linking to SWSEGrappling.attemptGrab().
resolutionNotes: A UI/action-metadata routing question (whether visible combat action rows carry resolutionMode/handler metadata linking to SWSEGrappling), not a calculated-number defect. Rounds 1-7 of the Math Integrity Freeze fixed and certified the underlying Grapple arithmetic, static/contextual modifier composition and stacking, the Reflex-vs-opposed-check channel split, opposed-check tie resolution, and the Grab attack's target-defense authority -- all reachable once a caller invokes SWSEGrappling's methods, regardless of which UI affordance does the invoking. Action-row wiring audit is out of scope for this freeze and remains deferred.

rule: Ion applies half damage to HP but compares original pre-halved Ion damage to Damage Threshold.
currentEvidence: DamageResolutionEngine currently appears to resolve from one damage number; ThresholdEngine comment says caller must pass correct Ion damage value.

rule: Special Ion CT/disable effects apply to droids, vehicles, electronic devices, and cybernetically enhanced creatures; not ordinary living creatures.
currentEvidence: No reliable target category/cybernetic eligibility check found in the damage resolution path.

rule: Eligible target moves -2 CT if original Ion damage equals/exceeds DT.
currentEvidence: ThresholdEngine generic threshold starts ctShift at 1; capIonDamageCtToOneStep exists but baseline Ion two-step shift was not found.
